paper.title: Minimal Exploration in Structured Stochastic Bandits

unmapped: Finite arm set X; parameter theta lies in a known compact set Theta encoding the structure; known observation family nu(theta(x)) and known (possibly unobserved, deterministic) reward map mu(x,theta)
settings.definition_quote: In each round, the decision maker selects an arm from a finite set $\cX$. Each arm $x\in\cX$ has an unknown parameter $\theta(x)\in \mathbb{R}$, and when this arm is chosen in round $t$, the decision maker observes a real-valued random variable $Y(x,t)$ with expectation $\theta(x)$ and distribution $\nu(\theta(x))$. ... The parameter $\theta$ lies in a compact set $\Theta$ that encodes the structural properties of the problem.

settings.name_in_paper: Generic structured stochastic MAB with Bernoulli observations
unmapped: Known compact parameter set Theta and known reward map mu(x,theta); learner solves the semi-infinite LP defining C(theta)

settings.name_in_paper: Generic structured stochastic MAB with Gaussian observations

source.label: th:low
source.quote: Let $\pi\in \Pi$ be a uniformly good algorithm. For any $\theta\in \Theta$, we have: \lim\inf_{T\to\infty} \frac{R^\pi(T,\theta)}{\ln~T} \ge C(\theta), where $C(\theta)$ is the value of the optimization problem: minimize \sum_{x} \eta(x) (\mu^\star(\theta) - \mu(x,\theta)) subject to \sum_{x} \eta(x) D( \theta, \lambda, x) \ge 1, \forall \lambda \in \Lambda(\theta)

results.notes: C(theta) is the Graves-Lai semi-infinite LP value, mapped to C_lin. Proof applies Graves & Lai (1997). Regret is defined via expectation of mu(x(t),theta), i.e. pseudo-regret.

symbols.F_eps_gamma: function F(epsilon, gamma, theta) with F -> 1 as epsilon, gamma -> 0; from the proof F = (1 + 2*epsilon*psi(theta)/C(theta))(1+gamma), psi(theta)=|X| ||c(theta)||_inf sum_x Delta(theta,x)

conditions: Assumption 4: KL divergence D continuous where finite
Assumption 6: unique solution of the optimization problem (2)-(3)

source.label: th:optimal
source.quote: If Assumptions~\ref{ass:unique}, \ref{as:div_continuous}, \ref{as:mu_continuous} and \ref{ass:unique_sol} hold and either Assumption~\ref{ass:bernoulli} or \ref{ass:gaussian} holds, then under the algorithm $\pi=$OSSB($\varepsilon,\gamma$) with $\varepsilon < {1 \over |\cX|}$ we have: \lim\sup_{T\to\infty} {R^\pi(T) \over \ln~T} \le C(\theta) F(\varepsilon,\gamma,\theta), with $F$ a function such that for all $\theta$, we have $F(\varepsilon,\gamma,\theta) \to 1$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ and $\gamma \to 0$.

results.notes: Asymptotically optimal (matches Theorem 1 as eps,gamma -> 0). The paper also states (informally, in Section 6 and the appendix proof) a finite-time bound R(T) <= mu*(theta)(G(gamma,|X|) + 2|X|/(eps delta(kappa)^2)) + (C(theta)(1+kappa)+2 eps psi(theta))(1+gamma) ln T. Computational cost depends on solving a semi-infinite LP each round; not stated to be polynomial.

symbols.F_eps_gamma: function F(epsilon, gamma, theta) with F -> 1 as epsilon, gamma -> 0; from the proof F = (1 + 2*epsilon*psi(theta)/C(theta))(1+gamma)
